label: first copy step echoing b (input b right after <DEL>) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at step L+1 (recall_idx 1), when the fed-back input is b, i.e. the first original token was b. Requires length L >= 6: none for L <= 5, weak and partial at L=6, always at L >= 7 (precision 1.0). Magnitude grows with L (L=9 carries 41% of mass, L=6 only 3%). A handful of weak activations for first token g. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at any other copy position, or for other first tokens.

issues: Minor: all 1095 test false positives (precision 0.90) come from L=6, where the feature fires only about 60% of the time (L==6 subset precision 0.603) and always weakly (bottom activation quartile, 2.5% of mass). The explanation already says this. No simple variable separates the L=6 firing cases from the non-firing ones: correct==1 gives 0.60, in_count==1 gives 0.65, out_tok a vowel gives 0.74, out_tok a digit gives 0.58. So this looks like graded, length-dependent strength rather than a missing condition.

Minor: the 127 missed activations (0.1% of mass) are almost all tiny activations (0.01-0.06 of max) at L=9 where the first token is g. This matches the claimed weak g activity (about 1% of activations) and is not a meaningful class.

Verified claims: activations occur only in the copy phase (recall_idx==1 holds 100% of mass) and never at L<=5. Mass share by L is 6: 2.6%, 7: 21.8%, 8: 34.5%, 9: 41.1%. The L>=7 version scores precision 1.0 and recall 0.82 on test. The version with no length condition scores F1 0.744 on test. The input b holds 99.9% of the mass.
